_note: STARTER catalogue of student misconceptions, tagged onto wrong options via `optionTags` in the quiz banks. Replace or extend with the errors you actually see (homework, exams, discussion sessions). 'description' is phrased as what the student believes; 'correct_idea' is reviewer/briefing text.

misconceptions.description: Photons from stimulated emission have random phase and direction, like spontaneous emission.
misconceptions.correct_idea: A stimulated photon is identical to the stimulating one: same frequency, phase, direction and polarization.

misconceptions.description: Strong enough pumping can produce population inversion in a two-level system.
misconceptions.correct_idea: Optical pumping of a two-level system can at best equalize the populations (transparency); inversion needs a 3- or 4-level scheme.

misconceptions.description: Population inversion (N2 > N1) alone is enough for laser oscillation; cavity losses do not matter.
misconceptions.correct_idea: Oscillation starts only when the gain compensates all losses, which needs an inversion above the critical value.

misconceptions.description: Doppler broadening is a homogeneous broadening mechanism.
misconceptions.correct_idea: Doppler broadening is inhomogeneous (atoms have different resonance frequencies); natural and collision broadening are homogeneous.

misconceptions.description: Saturating a homogeneously broadened line only depresses the gain near the saturating frequency (a spectral hole).
misconceptions.correct_idea: In a homogeneously broadened medium all atoms respond alike, so the whole gain line saturates uniformly; hole burning is characteristic of inhomogeneous broadening.

misconceptions.description: The rotating-wave approximation is valid for any detuning and any field strength.
misconceptions.correct_idea: It drops the fast counter-rotating term and holds near resonance with moderate coupling (Rabi frequency much smaller than the transition frequency).

misconceptions.description: The system matrix is the product with the first element the ray meets on the left.
misconceptions.correct_idea: M = Mn ... M2 M1: the last element the ray meets is leftmost.

misconceptions.description: A converging thin lens has C = +1/f.
misconceptions.correct_idea: In the standard convention the thin-lens matrix has C = -1/f for a converging lens (f > 0).

misconceptions.description: Matrices of successive elements are added to get the system matrix.
misconceptions.correct_idea: Successive elements combine by matrix multiplication, not addition.

misconceptions.description: Finesse increases with cavity length.
misconceptions.correct_idea: Finesse is set by the mirror reflectivity (and other losses), not by the spacing.

misconceptions.description: The free spectral range increases with cavity length.
misconceptions.correct_idea: FSR = c/(2nL) decreases as L grows.

misconceptions.description: The free spectral range is set by the mirror reflectivity rather than the mirror spacing.
misconceptions.correct_idea: FSR depends only on the optical round-trip length; reflectivity sets the finesse.

misconceptions.description: A two-mirror cavity is stable only if the mirror separation is smaller than the radius of curvature (L < R).
misconceptions.correct_idea: For two equal mirrors the stable range is L < 2R; the confocal case L = R lies inside it, not at its edge.

misconceptions.description: A negative g-parameter means the cavity is unstable.
misconceptions.correct_idea: Stability requires 0 < g1 g2 < 1; individual g values can be negative (two negative g give a positive product).

misconceptions.description: The g-parameter is g = L/R.
The wavefront is most strongly curved at the beam waist.
misconceptions.correct_idea: The wavefront is flat at the waist; its radius of curvature is smallest at z = +/- the Rayleigh range.

misconceptions.description: A higher cavity Q means a shorter photon lifetime.
misconceptions.correct_idea: Q = omega * tau_c, so higher Q means a longer photon lifetime (lower loss).

misconceptions.description: Above threshold the steady-state population inversion keeps increasing with the pump rate.
misconceptions.correct_idea: In steady state the inversion is clamped at the critical value; extra pump power goes into laser output.

misconceptions.description: Spatial hole burning only occurs in ring (travelling-wave) cavities.
misconceptions.correct_idea: It arises in standing-wave (linear) cavities, whose intensity nodes leave gain unsaturated.

misconceptions.description: A longer cavity makes single-mode operation easier.
misconceptions.correct_idea: A shorter cavity has a larger free spectral range, so fewer modes fall within the gain bandwidth.
